items.subject: Business Laws & Ethics (P5)
items.q: Mr. Sharma advertised a ₹5,000 reward for his lost bag. Kiran found it and offered to return it, but Mr. Sharma now refuses to pay. Kiran:
o: Can keep the bag and sue for the ₹5,000 reward
Has no claim at all against the owner
Can recover only his actual expenses
Can claim only if the police certify the return
items.why: A finder cannot sue for compensation in general, but where the owner has offered a specific reward, the finder can sue for it and may retain the goods until paid.
items.trap: The general rule (no right to sue for compensation) has an exception for a specifically offered reward.
items.source: CMA Inter MCQ Bank – Paper 5 (adapted)
items.exp: A finder cannot sue for compensation in general, but where the owner has offered a specific reward, the finder can sue for it and may retain the goods until paid.

items.subject: Financial Accounting (P6)
items.q: Stock worth ₹1,20,000 is insured for ₹90,000 with an average clause. Fire causes a loss of ₹60,000. The admissible claim is:
items.why: Claim = Loss × Policy value ÷ Value of stock = 60,000 × 90,000 ÷ 1,20,000 = ₹45,000.
items.trap: ₹60,000 ignores the average clause – the stock was under-insured.
items.source: CMA Inter MCQ Bank – Paper 6 (adapted)
items.exp: Claim = Loss × Policy value ÷ Value of stock = 60,000 × 90,000 ÷ 1,20,000 = ₹45,000.

items.subject: Direct Taxation (P7A)
items.q: Mr. John, a foreign citizen, visits India for the first time on 1 Oct 2025 and stays till 31 Mar 2026. His residential status for PY 2025-26 is:
items.why: He stays exactly 182 days (1 Oct–31 Mar), so he is Resident. As he was a non-resident in the earlier years, he is Resident but Not Ordinarily Resident.
items.trap: Count both arrival and departure days: 31 + 30 + 31 + 31 + 28 + 31 = 182.
items.source: CMA Inter MCQ Bank – Paper 7 (Sec A) (adapted)
items.exp: He stays exactly 182 days (1 Oct–31 Mar), so he is Resident. As he was a non-resident in the earlier years, he is Resident but Not Ordinarily Resident.

items.subject: Cost Accounting (P8)
items.q: Maximum usage 400 units/week, normal usage 300 units/week, maximum lead time 6 weeks, normal lead time 5 weeks. The re-order level is:
items.why: Re-order level = Maximum usage × Maximum lead time = 400 × 6 = 2,400 units.
items.trap: 1,500 uses normal figures – that is not the re-order level formula.
items.source: CMA Inter MCQ Bank – Paper 8 (adapted)
items.exp: Re-order level = Maximum usage × Maximum lead time = 400 × 6 = 2,400 units.

items.subject: Operations Management (P9A)
items.q: Design capacity is 60,000 units, effective capacity 50,000 units and actual output 45,000 units. The efficiency of the plant is:
items.why: Efficiency = Actual output ÷ Effective capacity = 45,000 ÷ 50,000 = 90%.
items.trap: 75% is utilisation (actual ÷ design capacity), not efficiency.
items.source: CMA Inter MCQ Bank – Paper 9 (Sec A) (adapted)
items.exp: Efficiency = Actual output ÷ Effective capacity = 45,000 ÷ 50,000 = 90%.

items.subject: Corporate Accounting (P10A)
items.q: ₹2,00,000 preference shares are redeemed at a 10% premium; ₹80,000 equity is issued at par for the purpose. The amount to be transferred to CRR is:
items.why: CRR = Nominal value redeemed − Proceeds of fresh issue = 2,00,000 − 80,000 = ₹1,20,000. The premium does not affect CRR.
items.trap: ₹1,40,000 wrongly adds the ₹20,000 premium.
items.source: CMA Inter MCQ Bank – Paper 10 (Sec A) (adapted)
items.exp: CRR = Nominal value redeemed − Proceeds of fresh issue = 2,00,000 − 80,000 = ₹1,20,000. The premium does not affect CRR.

items.subject: Financial Management (P11A)
items.q: Inventory period 45 days, receivables period 30 days and payables period 20 days. The NET operating cycle is:
items.why: Net operating cycle = 45 + 30 − 20 = 55 days.
items.trap: 75 days is the gross operating cycle – it ignores supplier credit.
items.source: CMA Inter MCQ Bank – Paper 11 (Sec A) (adapted)
items.exp: Net operating cycle = 45 + 30 − 20 = 55 days.

items.subject: Management Accounting (P12)
items.q: Selling price ₹40, variable cost ₹25 per unit, fixed cost ₹60,000, planned output 10,000 units. The break-even point is:
items.trap: Planned output of 10,000 units is irrelevant to the BEP.
items.source: CMA Inter MCQ Bank – Paper 12 (adapted)

items.subject: Business Laws & Ethics (P5)
items.q: An agreement with a minor is:
o: Voidable at the option of the minor
Valid if for the minor's benefit
Voidable at the option of the other party
items.why: An agreement with a minor is void from the beginning (Mohori Bibee v. Dharmodas Ghose).
items.trap: 'Voidable at the option of the minor' sounds protective, but the law treats it as void ab initio.
items.source: CMA Inter MCQ Bank – Paper 5 (adapted)
items.exp: An agreement with a minor is void from the beginning (Mohori Bibee v. Dharmodas Ghose).

items.subject: Financial Accounting (P6)
items.q: A bill drawn on 10 Jan 2026, payable 3 months after date, falls due on (assume no holiday):
items.why: 3 months after 10 Jan = 10 April; add 3 days of grace → 13 April 2026.
items.trap: Forgetting the 3 days of grace gives 10 April.
items.source: CMA Inter MCQ Bank – Paper 6 (adapted)
items.exp: 3 months after 10 Jan = 10 April; add 3 days of grace → 13 April 2026.

items.subject: Indirect Taxation (P7B)
items.q: A dealer sells a laptop with a carry bag in the same box at no separate charge, as is normal in the trade. For GST, this is:
o: A composite supply taxed at the laptop's rate
A mixed supply taxed at the highest rate
Laptop taxable, bag exempt as free
items.why: The items are naturally bundled with the laptop as the principal supply, so it is a composite supply taxed at the laptop's rate.
items.trap: Mixed supply applies only when items are NOT naturally bundled (e.g. a gift hamper).
items.source: CMA Inter MCQ Bank – Paper 7 (Sec B) (adapted)
items.exp: The items are naturally bundled with the laptop as the principal supply, so it is a composite supply taxed at the laptop's rate.

items.subject: Cost Accounting (P8)
items.q: Batch costing is most suitable for:
items.why: Batch costing suits industries producing identical units in lots, such as tablets in pharmaceuticals.
items.trap: Ship-building and bridges use contract costing; oil refining uses process costing.
items.source: CMA Inter MCQ Bank – Paper 8 (adapted)
items.exp: Batch costing suits industries producing identical units in lots, such as tablets in pharmaceuticals.

items.subject: Strategic Management (P9B)
items.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the four perspectives of the Balanced Scorecard?
items.why: The four perspectives are Financial, Customer, Internal Business Process, and Learning & Growth.
items.trap: 'Competitor' sounds strategic, but it is not one of the four.
items.source: CMA Inter MCQ Bank – Paper 9 (Sec B) (adapted)
items.exp: The four perspectives are Financial, Customer, Internal Business Process, and Learning & Growth.

items.subject: Auditing (P10B)
items.q: A company's Board wants its statutory auditor to also advise on investing surplus funds, for a separate fee. Under the Companies Act, 2013 this is:
o: Allowed if the fee is below the audit fee
items.why: Section 144 prohibits an auditor from rendering investment advisory services to the company, directly or indirectly. No approval makes it permissible.
items.trap: Board/Audit Committee approval is for OTHER permitted services, not prohibited ones.
items.source: CMA Inter MCQ Bank – Paper 10 (Sec B) (adapted)
items.exp: Section 144 prohibits an auditor from rendering investment advisory services to the company, directly or indirectly. No approval makes it permissible.

items.subject: Business Data Analytics (P11B)
items.q: XBRL stands for:
items.why: XBRL = eXtensible Business Reporting Language, a standard format for electronic business and financial reporting.
items.trap: 'Recording' looks right for accounting, but XBRL is about reporting.
items.source: CMA Inter MCQ Bank – Paper 11 (Sec B) (adapted)
items.exp: XBRL = eXtensible Business Reporting Language, a standard format for electronic business and financial reporting.

items.subject: Management Accounting (P12)
items.q: Fixed cost ₹24,000, P/V ratio 40% and desired profit ₹20,000. Sales required to earn this profit are:
items.why: Required sales = (Fixed cost + Desired profit) ÷ P/V ratio = 44,000 ÷ 40% = ₹1,10,000.
items.trap: Dividing only the profit (₹50,000) ignores the fixed cost.
items.source: CMA Inter MCQ Bank – Paper 12 (adapted)
items.exp: Required sales = (Fixed cost + Desired profit) ÷ P/V ratio = 44,000 ÷ 40% = ₹1,10,000.

items.subject: Business Laws & Ethics (P5)
items.topic: Sale by person with voidable title
items.q: A obtained a car from B by fraud and, before B rescinded the contract, sold it to C, who bought in good faith without notice of the fraud. C:
o: Gets no title as A obtained it by fraud
Gets title only if B agrees
Must return the car to B
items.why: A buyer gets good title from a seller holding goods under a voidable contract if it was not rescinded at the time of sale and the buyer acted in good faith.
items.trap: If B had rescinded the contract BEFORE the sale to C, C would not get a good title.
items.source: CMA Inter MCQ Bank – Paper 5 (adapted)
items.exp: A buyer gets good title from a seller holding goods under a voidable contract if it was not rescinded at the time of sale and the buyer acted in good faith.

items.subject: Financial Accounting (P6)
items.q: Debtors: opening ₹45,000, closing ₹60,000. Cash received ₹3,00,000, discount allowed ₹12,000, bad debts ₹8,000, returns inward ₹5,000. Credit sales are:
items.trap: Leaving out returns inward gives ₹3,35,000.
items.source: CMA Inter MCQ Bank – Paper 6 (adapted)

items.subject: Direct Taxation (P7A)
items.q: Ravi receives ₹30,000 and ₹25,000 from two friends and ₹40,000 from his brother in the same year. The amount taxable is:
items.why: The ₹50,000 limit applies to the aggregate of gifts from non-relatives: 55,000 > 50,000, so the whole ₹55,000 is taxable. The brother's gift is exempt.
items.trap: The limit is tested on the total, and once crossed the entire amount (not just the excess) is taxable.
items.source: CMA Inter MCQ Bank – Paper 7 (Sec A) (adapted)
items.exp: The ₹50,000 limit applies to the aggregate of gifts from non-relatives: 55,000 > 50,000, so the whole ₹55,000 is taxable. The brother's gift is exempt.

items.subject: Cost Accounting (P8)
items.q: Input 8,000 units, normal loss 10% of input, actual output 7,000 units. The abnormal loss is:
items.why: Expected output = 8,000 − 800 = 7,200. Abnormal loss = 7,200 − 7,000 = 200 units.
items.trap: 1,000 units is the total loss; 800 of it is normal.
items.source: CMA Inter MCQ Bank – Paper 8 (adapted)
items.exp: Expected output = 8,000 − 800 = 7,200. Abnormal loss = 7,200 − 7,000 = 200 units.

items.subject: Operations Management (P9A)
items.q: 15 workers produce 450 units in a month of 25 working days. Labour productivity per worker per month is:
items.why: Productivity per worker per month = 450 ÷ 15 = 30 units.
items.trap: 1.2 is per worker per DAY (30 ÷ 25).
items.source: CMA Inter MCQ Bank – Paper 9 (Sec A) (adapted)
items.exp: Productivity per worker per month = 450 ÷ 15 = 30 units.

items.subject: Corporate Accounting (P10A)
items.q: As per amended Schedule III, current maturities of long-term borrowings are shown under:
items.why: Since the 2021 amendment, current maturities of long-term borrowings are shown under 'Short-term borrowings'.
items.trap: 'Other current liabilities' was the pre-amendment position in older books.
items.source: CMA Inter MCQ Bank – Paper 10 (Sec A) (adapted)
items.exp: Since the 2021 amendment, current maturities of long-term borrowings are shown under 'Short-term borrowings'.

items.subject: Financial Management (P11A)
items.q: Current ratio is 2.5 : 1 and net working capital is ₹6,00,000. Current assets are:
items.trap: ₹4,00,000 is the current liabilities.
items.source: CMA Inter MCQ Bank – Paper 11 (Sec A) (adapted)

items.subject: Management Accounting (P12)
items.q: A division has operating profit ₹40 lakh, operating assets ₹2 crore and cost of capital 14%. Its residual income is:
items.why: Residual income = 40 − (200 × 14%) = 40 − 28 = ₹12 lakh.
items.trap: ₹28 lakh is the capital charge; 20% is the ROI.
items.source: CMA Inter MCQ Bank – Paper 12 (adapted)
items.exp: Residual income = 40 − (200 × 14%) = 40 − 28 = ₹12 lakh.

items.subject: Business Laws & Ethics (P5)
items.q: A public company has 4,200 members. Unless the articles require more, the quorum for its general meeting is:
items.why: Public company: up to 1,000 members – 5; more than 1,000 up to 5,000 – 15; more than 5,000 – 30.
items.trap: Proxies do not count towards quorum – only members personally present.
items.source: CMA Inter MCQ Bank – Paper 5 (adapted)
items.exp: Public company: up to 1,000 members – 5; more than 1,000 up to 5,000 – 15; more than 5,000 – 30.

items.subject: Financial Accounting (P6)
items.q: A machine costing ₹5,00,000 is depreciated at 20% p.a. on WDV. Depreciation for the 3rd year is:
items.trap: ₹1,00,000 every year would be the straight-line method.
items.source: CMA Inter MCQ Bank – Paper 6 (adapted)

items.subject: Indirect Taxation (P7B)
items.q: Machinery is imported by air: FOB US$10,000, exchange rate ₹85/US$. Air freight and insurance cannot be ascertained. The assessable value is:
items.trap: ₹10,31,475 takes insurance on FOB + freight; it is 1.125% of FOB only.
items.source: CMA Inter MCQ Bank – Paper 7 (Sec B) (adapted)

items.subject: Cost Accounting (P8)
items.q: Workers at the beginning 180, at the end 220; 20 workers left during the year. Labour turnover by the separation method is:
items.trap: Dividing by the opening (11.11%) or closing (9.09%) strength instead of the average.
items.source: CMA Inter MCQ Bank – Paper 8 (adapted)

items.subject: Strategic Management (P9B)
items.q: For an electric-scooter maker, a new government subsidy on EV purchases is best classified in SWOT as a/an:
items.why: A government subsidy is an external, favourable factor – an Opportunity. Strengths and weaknesses are internal.
items.trap: It helps the company, so students tick 'Strength' – but it is not an internal capability.
items.source: CMA Inter MCQ Bank – Paper 9 (Sec B) (adapted)
items.exp: A government subsidy is an external, favourable factor – an Opportunity. Strengths and weaknesses are internal.

items.subject: Auditing (P10B)
items.q: An arrangement where one clerk's work is automatically checked by another clerk in the normal course of work is called:
items.why: Internal check divides duties so that one person's work is automatically checked by another, preventing or detecting errors and frauds.
items.trap: Internal audit is a separate review done after the work, not a built-in automatic check.
items.source: CMA Inter MCQ Bank – Paper 10 (Sec B) (adapted)
items.exp: Internal check divides duties so that one person's work is automatically checked by another, preventing or detecting errors and frauds.

items.subject: Business Data Analytics (P11B)
items.q: Individual bill entries recorded at a billing counter, before any processing, are best described as:
items.why: Data are raw, unprocessed facts; once processed and organised (e.g. a sales summary) they become information.
items.trap: A sales REPORT would be information; unprocessed entries are data.
items.source: CMA Inter MCQ Bank – Paper 11 (Sec B) (adapted)
items.exp: Data are raw, unprocessed facts; once processed and organised (e.g. a sales summary) they become information.

items.subject: Management Accounting (P12)
items.q: Sales: Feb ₹1,00,000, Mar ₹1,20,000. 40% are cash sales; credit sales are collected in the next month. Cash received in March is:
items.trap: ₹1,12,000 swaps the months – March's credit sales are collected in April.
items.source: CMA Inter MCQ Bank – Paper 12 (adapted)

items.subject: Business Laws & Ethics (P5)
items.q: An LLP's two designated partners both live abroad and stayed in India for only 40 days in the financial year. The LLP:
o: Complies – two designated partners are enough
Complies – NRIs are treated as residents
Does not comply – all partners must be designated
Does not comply – at least one must be resident in India
items.why: Every LLP needs at least two designated partners who are individuals, at least one of whom is resident in India (stayed at least 120 days in the financial year).
items.trap: Having two designated partners is not enough by itself – the residence condition must also be met.
items.source: CMA Inter MCQ Bank – Paper 5 (adapted)
items.exp: Every LLP needs at least two designated partners who are individuals, at least one of whom is resident in India (stayed at least 120 days in the financial year).

items.subject: Financial Accounting (P6)
items.q: Goods are invoiced to the consignee at cost + 25%. Unsold stock at invoice price is ₹50,000. The stock reserve required is:
items.trap: ₹12,500 takes 25% of the invoice price; use 25/125 on invoice price.
items.source: CMA Inter MCQ Bank – Paper 6 (adapted)

items.subject: Direct Taxation (P7A)
items.q: Mr. Das earns ₹5,00,000 from growing and manufacturing tea in India. The amount taxable as business income is:
items.why: For tea grown and manufactured, 60% is agricultural income (exempt) and 40% is business income: 40% × 5,00,000 = ₹2,00,000.
items.trap: Tea is 60:40; rubber is 65:35 and coffee (grown and cured) is 75:25 – don't mix them up.
items.source: CMA Inter MCQ Bank – Paper 7 (Sec A) (adapted)
items.exp: For tea grown and manufactured, 60% is agricultural income (exempt) and 40% is business income: 40% × 5,00,000 = ₹2,00,000.

items.subject: Cost Accounting (P8)
items.q: Supplier P quotes ₹2.50 per unit. Supplier Q quotes ₹2.30 per unit plus ₹4,000 fixed. Cost is the same from both at:
items.why: Indifference point = 4,000 ÷ (2.50 − 2.30) = 20,000 units.
items.trap: Above 20,000 units Supplier Q is cheaper; below it Supplier P is cheaper.
items.source: CMA Inter MCQ Bank – Paper 8 (adapted)
items.exp: Indifference point = 4,000 ÷ (2.50 − 2.30) = 20,000 units.

items.subject: Operations Management (P9A)
items.q: Path A–B–D takes 15 days and path A–C–D takes 12 days. The slack available on activity C is:
items.why: The critical path is the longest (15 days). C lies only on the 12-day path, so its slack = 15 − 12 = 3 days.
items.trap: Only activities on the critical path have zero slack.
items.source: CMA Inter MCQ Bank – Paper 9 (Sec A) (adapted)
items.exp: The critical path is the longest (15 days). C lies only on the 12-day path, so its slack = 15 − 12 = 3 days.

items.subject: Corporate Accounting (P10A)
items.q: 1 Apr 2025: 10,000 shares. 1 Oct 2025: 4,000 shares issued for cash. 1 Jan 2026: 2,000 shares bought back. Weighted average shares for FY 2025-26 are:
items.trap: Shares count only for the period they were outstanding.
items.source: CMA Inter MCQ Bank – Paper 10 (Sec A) (adapted)

items.subject: Financial Management (P11A)
items.q: 12% irredeemable debentures of ₹100 each are issued at ₹96. Tax rate is 30%. The after-tax cost of debt is:
items.trap: 8.40% divides by face value (₹100) instead of net proceeds (₹96).
items.source: CMA Inter MCQ Bank – Paper 11 (Sec A) (adapted)

items.subject: Management Accounting (P12)
items.q: Set-up cost pool ₹6,00,000; expected 2,500 set-ups. Product D needs 1,000 set-ups. Set-up overhead charged to Product D is:
items.trap: Splitting the pool equally (₹3,00,000) ignores the cost driver.
items.source: CMA Inter MCQ Bank – Paper 12 (adapted)
